assessment:
The table sees Goblin Matron enter and assumes you went and got a lord. Let them assume it, then go and get the removal instead — Matron searches for a Goblin CARD, and both Gempalm Incinerator and Boggart Shenanigans wear that word. Two wishes, one creature type, and every wish is on plan.

Know the split cold, because it decides which card you name. Matron delivers to your hand, so the fetch still has to be cast — and kicker still works. Moggcatcher puts a Goblin permanent straight onto the battlefield, so there is no cast, no counterspell window, and no kicker. Send finishers to hand. Send engines to the battlefield.

Moggcatcher taps to do it, so he does nothing the turn he lands. Deploy him a full rotation before you want the wish, on a turn nobody is watching you. And stop planning to cast and activate him in the same turn — your mean available mana does not reach the seven that would take at any point in ten turns.

Neither wish touches the spell half of this deck, and that is fine. Wish for bodies and engines; let Zada's copied cantrips find the rest (stack 001).

targets.scenario: The default. Turn 4-5, three or four Goblins on the battlefield, Goblin Warchief down or in hand, and nobody at the table pointing anything at you yet.
targets.why: Take the burst, and build the whole turn around exactly one activation. Stack 004 walks it: under Warchief he costs {1}{R}{R}, arrives with haste, and taps the turn he lands — five Goblins become ten, 13 hasted power. Matron hands him over, so you cast him on your turn with the haste line intact. Never feed him to Skirk Prospector expecting him back.

targets.scenario: Behind. The board just got wrathed, you are rebuilding on four lands, and a second sweeper is entirely plausible.
targets.why: Rebuild with the cheap card, not the best one. Marshal is three bodies on one card — a token when he enters, another when he dies — and the goldfish only has you back to 4.07 bodies by turn five, so he beats the whole rebuild curve by himself. Let the echo lapse when you want the second token now; pay it when the body is doing real blocking.

targets.scenario: Closing. A wide board and a lethal you can already count, and you need the team hasted this turn rather than next.
targets.why: Name him and pay the kicker: your creatures get +1/+0 and haste the moment he enters. This is the wish only Matron can grant, because kicker is paid as you cast the spell — Moggcatcher would put an unkicked 1/1 onto the battlefield and hand you nothing. Count the damage before you fetch, not after.

targets.scenario: The one nobody sees coming. An opposing lord or a must-die blocker is holding your swarm hostage and your hand is all gas, no answers.
targets.why: Pull removal out of a creature tutor. Cycle him for {1}{R} to deal damage equal to the number of Goblins on the battlefield — count their Goblins too, they add to it — and draw a card while you do it. Cycling only works from hand, so route this wish through Matron every time and never through Moggcatcher.

tutors.notes: Once the errand is run, Matron is a Goblin body: count her for Krenko, tap her for Brightstone Ritual, feed her to Prospector. And she finds Goblin cards, not Goblin creatures — Boggart Shenanigans is a Kindred Enchantment, and it is a perfectly legal wish on a grinding table.

targets.scenario: The default. Moggcatcher untapped from last turn, three mana spare, a Goblin board, and a haste lord already down — Warchief, Chieftain or Howlsquad Heavy.
targets.why: Skip the cast entirely and give the table nothing to counter: there is no spell here, only the ability. With the haste lord already down he taps immediately for the stack 004 burst, five Goblins into ten. Without one he is next turn's doubling — on that board fetch something else and take Krenko when the lord arrives.

targets.scenario: Behind. A stax artifact is throttling your spell count, or a Treasure deck is running away with the table.
targets.why: Go and get the repeatable out, and do it on the end step before your turn — this is an activated ability, so the wish happens at instant speed. Trashmaster sacrifices a Goblin to destroy target artifact, again and again, and buffs the team while he waits. Break the first lock piece cheaply; it is the second and third that actually end you.

targets.scenario: Closing. Impact Tremors on the battlefield, an opponent in single digits, three mana and an untapped Moggcatcher.
targets.why: Win without declaring an attack. One activation puts four bodies onto the battlefield — the Commander plus three tokens — so Impact Tremors deals 4 to each opponent immediately, and then every spare Goblin converts at {1}{R} into 2 damage anywhere you point it. Fetch him on the board where blockers are the only reason you have not won.

targets.scenario: The one nobody sees coming. A grinding table where your Goblins die in bulk every rotation, and you want reach that survives the next sweeper.
targets.why: Use a creature tutor to put an enchantment onto the battlefield — Shenanigans is a Kindred Enchantment, so Moggcatcher may legally go and get it, and nobody defends against that. Every Goblin funeral afterwards is a point of damage at any player. Fetch it before you cast Blasphemous Act, never after, and turn your own reset into a burn spell.

tutors.notes: The trap to never walk into: a permanent put onto the battlefield was never cast, so a fetched Goblin Bushwhacker enters unkicked — no pump, no haste, no kill. Finishers through Matron, engines through Moggcatcher. And Moggcatcher is a Human Mercenary, so neither tutor can find him, he adds nothing to Krenko's count, and Prospector cannot eat him.

gaps: Both wishes are Goblin-shaped, so the spell half of the list is unfetchable — nothing here finds Impact Tremors, Skullclamp, a ritual or a storm payoff. Stop waiting on a tutor to assemble the big turn: storm payoff plus ritual shows up in 15.2% of goldfish games and neither of these cards moves that number by a point. Assemble it the other way, through Zada's copied cantrips, Faithless Looting and Idol of Oblivion, and spend the wishes on the bodies those copies need. The turn the payoff is already in your hand is the turn a wish is worth the most — fetch the board, not the spell.
